questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
The diagram shows a country’s production possibility curve. N good Y M O good X What could allow the economy to move from M to N in the long run?

options.B: an increase in demand for exports
options.C: an increase in government spending on pensions

questions.questionText: Which statement about factors of production is correct?

options.A: All factors of production can earn income for their owner.
options.B: The factor capital includes human capital, money capital and physical capital.
options.C: The factor labour involves only physical effort.
options.D: The natural resources classed as land are in unlimited supply.

options.D: D O O quantity of gold rings quantity of gold rings

questions.questionText: Which combination of changes could leave the position of the demand curve for a normal good X unchanged?

options.A: a decrease in taste for product X and a decrease in the quality of product Y for which product X is a complement
options.B: a decrease in the quality of a substitute and an increase in incomes
options.C: an increase in the price of a substitute and an increase in population size
options.D: an increase in the price of product Y for which product X is a complement and a successful advertising campaign for product X

questions.questionText: A product has a normal demand curve and a normal supply curve. What would explain a rise in the price of the product and a fall in the quantity of the product traded?

options.A: The decrease in demand is double the decrease in supply.
options.B: The decrease in supply is double the decrease in demand.
options.C: The increase in demand is double the increase in supply.
options.D: The increase in supply is double the increase in demand.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows how the quantity demanded of four goods changes as income changes. Which good has an income elasticity of demand which is always +1?

options.A: B C quantity of good D demanded O income

questions.questionText: The cross elasticity of demand between bus travel and rail travel is +2. A rise in the price of bus fares caused the demand for rail travel to rise by 10%. Which change in bus fares has brought this about? from to (cents) (cents)

The supply function for a good can be written as Q = 2P + 10, where Q is the quantity supplied in kilos and P is the price per kilo in dollars. The price rises from $10 to $15 per kilo. The value of price elasticity of supply for this price increase lies in a range from

options.A: 1 to 1 . B 3 to 1 . C 2 to 3 . D 1 1 to 11 .

Which situation would indicate the presence of an externality?

options.A: Producers’ actions cause a shortage of a particular good.
options.B: Private motorists contribute to traffic congestion in city centres.
options.C: Differences in ability cause inequality in the distribution of income in an economy.

questions.questionText: A local council charges for the use of tennis courts but not for the use of street lights. How would an economist explain this?

options.A: Tennis courts are a luxury but street lights are a necessity.
options.B: Tennis courts are worth more than street lights.
options.C: There is an opportunity cost of using land to build tennis courts but not street lights.
options.D: The use of street lights cannot be restricted.

questions.questionText: The government is considering building flood defences along a river. It has calculated the costs and benefits as follows. costs benefits $m $m private 450 260 external 60 190 According to cost-benefit analysis, which decision and reasoning about flood defences is correct? decision reasoning

options.A: build external benefits are greater than external costs
options.B: build social benefits are greater than private benefits
options.C: do not build private costs are greater than the external benefits
options.D: do not build social costs are greater than the social benefits

questions.questionText: In the diagram, MN is the production possibility curve of a country that has a comparative advantage in the production of good Y. M R quantity of good X O N quantity of good Y What might enable the country to consume the quantities of X and Y indicated by point R?

options.A: increased specialisation in the production of good X
options.D: increased specialisation in the production of good Y

questions.questionText: A country is willing to undertake free trade with its neighbours and to allow the free movement of factors of production with them. It is unwilling, however, to share a common currency and common external tariff. In what sort of economic relationship is it likely to be with its neighbours?
Which combination of price changes must cause an improvement in the country’s terms of trade? average price average price of exports of imports

options.B: interest charges on a loan from a US based international bank
options.C: investment by the parent company in the plant’s assembly line
options.D: profits remitted to the Japanese parent company
